changelog: Add an Order Principle that prefers the later cut when multiple candidates all fall before the same sentence-final inflection, so decisions favour preserving the predicate, tense/aspect/negation and avoid misattachment (addresses the primary finding).
findings: When several cuts all fall before the same sentence‑final inflection, the prompt fails to choose which is least harmful: the later cut (closer to the inflection) preserves more of the predicate and is preferable.
The prompt allows cuts that separate a predicate from its sentence‑final inflection (tense/negation/politeness), producing contradictory or unusable fragments.

edits.now: When multiple candidates fall before the same sentence‑final inflection, prefer

diagnosis.why: The new Order Principle (prefer the later cut among candidates before the same sentence-final inflection) changed which positions are ranked top‑1 versus top‑2/3: rank_depth fell at depth‑1 (−0.419) while improving depths 2–4, so the edit shuffled the very top choice and harmed short budgets and overall H_set (by_bin shows larger drops for longer bins). Concretely, it caused cuts to be placed inside phrases or before punctuation in some sentences (splitting pronouns/particles or detaching punctuation), producing the large negative tail movements.
diagnosis.lesson: Constrain the Order Principle so it never chooses cuts that split tokens/close dependents or move the single top choice for short-latency budgets; verify effects separately on top‑1 and long‑budget bins.
